Definition: properly, to try, i.e. (by implication) select
BiblicalUsage: Bachar means to choose — to try and then select. God chose Israel above all people on the face of the earth, he chose David his servant and took him from the sheepfolds, Joshua said choose you this day whom ye will serve, and Isaiah says the Lord's servant is mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth. The same word for choosing a king, a people, and a Saviour.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe choosing is the heart of the covenant: God chose Israel when she was nothing, and he chose me the same way. And I hold that my own choosing answers his — choose you this day whom ye will serve, and I choose the Lord.
